How this board works

  • Notes (left) stay put while you pan and zoom and save themselves as you type. Drag the bottom-right corner to resize; click the title to fold. Everything is also written into content/_board_thumbs/board_notes.txt — connect it once with Connect board_notes.txt; after a Chrome restart one click on the notes reconnects it.
  • One column per run (one Genjutsu motion-transfer generation), videos left to right, oldest first. A video split into two runs has two columns under one heading. Read each column top to bottom: 1 Reference → 2 New woman + room → 3 Final video; the rows line up across the whole board.
  • Two approvals per run. The references first: REFS FOR REVIEW → REFS APPROVED — nothing is generated before that. Then our clip: CLIP FOR REVIEW → APPROVED (or REJECTED → re-rolled as the next take). ▶ Side by side plays the reference and our clip together.
  • Approve / Reject appear only where something waits for you. Each click copies one line for Claude; Review (bottom right) dims everything else; Copy decisions copies all your lines at once — paste them to Claude.

Bra references — attached to every run

Open questions before generating

  1. Product photos. Keep the Pinterest bra pictures above, or send the supplier's photos.

  3. Colour switching. Videos 2, 4, 7, 9 and 10 change bra colour on every cut. The prompts list the colour per cut, but it is the riskiest part for motion transfer.
  4. Sound. Genjutsu keeps the reference's own audio (voices included) — replace it in CapCut.

@Video1 is the motion source. @Image1 is the new woman. @Image2 is the room. @Image3 shows the leopard bra from the front. @Image4 shows the back of the leopard bra, showing the keyhole cut-out and the crossed straps. Use @Video1 only for motion, camera and timing: keep every shot, every cut, every camera move, pose, gesture, hand movement and head turn, with its exact timing, as in @Video1, in the same vertical 9:16 framing, with the woman at the same position, distance and size in frame. Recast the woman as the woman from @Image1: a woman in her late thirties with shoulder-length layered chestnut-brown hair, light green eyes and a slim, toned figure. Take only her face, hair, skin and body from @Image1; her clothes come from this prompt. In every shot she wears plain dark jeans on her lower body. The garment she puts on is the posture corrector bra shown in @Image3 and @Image4. It is seamless and wire-free, with a deep V neckline, wide shoulder straps and smooth moulded cups; the back is open with a large rounded keyhole cut-out under the shoulder blades; two long elastic straps hang from the back panel, cross behind her back and close at the front under the bust with a short hook-and-eye band. In this whole clip the bra is leopard and only leopard: brown leopard print with black spots, with the same leopard print on the shoulder straps, the back panel, the long straps and the hook band. It is the same leopard bra in every shot, from the first frame to the last, and it never changes colour, even where the bra in @Video1 has a different colour or pattern. It moves exactly as the bra moves in @Video1. Keep both shots of @Video1. In the first shot she wears a plain leopard-print strapless bandeau and holds the folded leopard posture bra up in front of her, showing it to the camera while she talks. After the cut she pulls the posture bra down over her head like a top, arms up, and settles the shoulder straps, the long back straps still hanging loose. Every shot takes place in the room from @Image2: a cosy farmhouse bedroom: white shiplap walls, a rustic wooden bed with cream bedding and a chunky knit throw, floating shelves with plants and books, a window with soft daylight. The camera sees the room from where the phone stands in @Video1, with the woman standing in the open floor space, and the same light direction in every shot. Hyperrealistic, natural, unedited iPhone video filmed at home in ordinary daylight, like a real person's TikTok: real skin with pores, small imperfections and natural shine; no beauty filter, no skin smoothing, no glow, no cinematic colour grading; real cotton and elastic fabric with creases and folds; natural white balance and true-to-life colours, with the slight softness and sensor noise of a phone camera. No text of any kind anywhere in the frame: no on-screen captions, no subtitles, no emojis, no stickers, no text overlays, no logos, no watermarks.

Known problem

In the black run Genjutsu kept the white T-shirt the woman wears in her picture and put the bra over it; in the nude run she has bare skin under the bra. So the T-shirt appears and disappears on the colour cuts. Her hair is also shorter in the black shots. And in the nude run's second shot (1.04–3.42 s) she turns her back to the camera, where the reel has her facing it with her hands at the nape. Fix: re-run the black shots asking for nothing under the bra (may be refused — free), or accept.

Why one generation per bra colour

Hyperrealism

Why take 5 is made this way
Why one generation per bra colour

Take 1 (one run over the whole reel, colours as time codes in the prompt) turned the leopard bra nude at 1.8 s in the middle of a shot, with no cut. Genjutsu does not follow time codes for the garment colour. Now each run gets only the reel's shots of ONE colour, joined into one driving video (v9_c01_r4.mp4 leopard, r5 nude + one black shot as filler, r6 black), and only that colour's product pictures (back views cropped per colour from references/bra_back_three_colours.png). Same woman and room as take 1.
